author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Building a 2D Platformer on the PlayStation 2 - Streaming Level Chunks and VRAM
summary: A later PS2 homebrew stream applies resource streaming to a real 2D platformer, loading level chunks into VRAM while debugging framebuffer and video problems that emerge when an engine stops treating the whole level as static.

blocks.text: The session moves beyond an isolated texture upload test by making chunk streaming serve an actual level. The creator loads portions of a 2D platformer into VRAM as the player progresses, while confronting framebuffer behavior and unresolved video faults. That application reveals the coordination cost hidden by a simple demo: chunk boundaries, asset lifetime, camera movement and graphics-memory reuse must agree. A dated stream and public `ps2-simple-platformer` repository provide a traceable snapshot of the project while those systems are still evolving.

At more than two and a half hours, the video includes exploratory debugging rather than a distilled final architecture. Its metadata leaves out chunk size, memory budget, load latency and a completed performance target. Some observed faults may belong to temporary code rather than the PS2 hardware model. Its value is precisely that unfinished engineering context, but conclusions should be tied to the linked revision. It complements lower-level DMA material without replacing a documented asset format or production-ready streaming design.
